subject: Film & Cinema
title: Documentary: Truth Through a Lens
description: A short lesson to help you apply Documentary: Truth Through a Lens.

hook.text: Documentaries claim to show reality. But every cut is a choice, and every choice is a bias.

buildup.text: From Nanook of the North to Making a Murderer, docs shape how we see the real world.

discovery.text: Editing, music, and interview framing can make the same facts tell opposite stories.

twist.text: True-crime docs have overturned convictions — proving documentaries can change lives.

climax.text: The line between documentary and propaganda depends on who's holding the camera.

punchline.text: Objectivity is the biggest fiction in nonfiction.

quiz.question: Why are documentaries not purely objective?
options: Editing and framing choices introduce the filmmaker's bias
